rendered: After 1500[1] cycles at the higher rate, the cathode delivers 306 mAh[2] per gram of sulfur. Per gram of the whole electrode, it delivers 87 mAh/g[3] after 1500[4] cycles at 100%[5] depth of discharge. Dividing the electrode-level value by the sulfur-level value gives an implied sulfur share of 28.4%[6] of the electrode. This is somewhat below the sulfur content the paper states, which is 35 wt % active sulfur[7] (a moderate loading). The gap likely reflects the electrode-level basis, since the electrode mass also includes carbon, binder, and other non-sulfur components.
